title: biomethanol startup emvolon signs purchasing financing deals with freepoint 2026 08 27
text:
NEW YORK, Aug 27 (Reuters) - Biomethanol startup Emvolon has signed a seven-year deal under which trader Freepoint Commodities will have a first purchase option on liquid fuels ​and the right of first refusal on investing in its projects, the ‌company said on Thursday.
Emvolon valued the purchase option at $450 million.
The deal could help Emvolon solve one of the biggest challenges for alternative fuel projects. Investors and financiers have long been on the ​sidelines, unwilling to risk betting on nascent technologies that are not guaranteed to ​have dedicated buyers for them.
For Stamford, Connecticut-based Freepoint, it gives the ⁠trading house preferential access and guaranteed supply of a commodity that is expected to ​play a role in the decarbonization of shipping, aviation and other heavily polluting industries.
Emvolon's ​business is built around repurposing car engines to produce biomethanol at sites where methane gas is generated from waste, such as landfills, agricultural waste processors and fossil fuel production sites, a model that ​it claims is more cost-effective than building large chemical plants.
Adoption of low-carbon methanol has ​been slower than expected due to high cost of supply and regulatory uncertainty, which earlier this ‌year ⁠forced SunGas Renewables to scrap a planned low-carbon methanol facility in Louisiana using wood fiber. SunGas also cited lack of clarity on financing.
Placing production next to the feedstock - waste gas - helps reduce transportation and other logistics costs, Emvolon's Chief Executive Officer Emmanuel Kasseris ​told Reuters in an ​interview.
"A lot of ⁠feedstock is wasted in the United States because there is no way to get it to chemical plants," Kasseris said. "We solve ​that problem by getting the production to the feedstock, instead of ​having to ⁠aggregate and transport that."
Emvolon's first production site is expected to begin output in the first half of next year and scale to about 4,000 to 5,000 metric tons a ⁠year, Kasseris ​said.
It plans to scale total production to 300,000 ​tons annually by ramping up at the first site at a Montauk Renewables (MNTK.O)
